newsitem.title: SLOVENIA: Slovenia seeks Italian support for EU, NATO bids.
newsitem.headline: Slovenia seeks Italian support for EU, NATO bids.

text.p: Slovenia's government, preparing for a visit by Italian Prime Minister Romano Prodi, said on Monday it hoped Italy would support its bid to join the European Union (EU) and NATO as soon as possible.
Prodi, expected to arrive in Slovenia late on Monday, is scheduled to meet his counterpart Janez Drnovsek, President Milan Kucan and parliamentary president Janez Podobnik.

"Particular attention will be paid to Slovenia's incorporation into NATO and the European Union, (and) to the strengthening of economic, regional and cross-border cooperation," the Foreign Ministry said in a statement.

"In its efforts to secure Slovenia's entry into NATO in the first round of expansion, the Slovene government greatly values the support expressed on a number of occasions by Italy and in particular by Prime Minister Prodi," it added.
Slovenia is widely seen as the best-placed outsider to win early NATO membership in alliance's first round of expansion, possibly before the end of the year.

Slovenia also hopes to become a member of the EU as soon as possible. Improved relations with Italy were the key factor that led to the signing of Slovenia's association agreement with the EU in June 1996, following years of negotiations.
Before Prodi came to power last April, Italy was blocking Slovenia's EU agreement over Slovenia's refusal to hand back property confiscated from ethnic Italians after World War Two.
"As an influential member of the EU, Italy can make a positive contribution to the early acceptance of Slovenia as a full member of the EU," it added.
The association agreement has yet to be ratified by Slovenian and most EU member governments.
Italy is Slovenia's second major trading partner, accounting for about 20 percent of its foreign trade.
